title: Alan Drew, the filthy M.C., and Redd Foxx
summary: Whaley recalls Alan Drew's quick repartee, and they compare him to modern foul-mouthed comics such as Redd Foxx and Richard Pryor.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: know, if anybody would heckle her, she'd stop and fire right back at them. Alan Drew, you remember him?
Alan Drew, he sang -- yeah, tell me about Alan.
He was an M.C.
You ran into all these show people.
Oh, yeah.

That's what we really want to know about, Tom. The people that the people of the world don't know about now, because they're gone. And they don't know that these were the people that basically were before the Billy Eckstein's and the Lou Rawls and the Johnny Mathis and the Sammy Davis's. So you tell me now, who was this guy?

Alan Drew was an M.C. Milton Berle used to come up to the theater every day and sit there and listen to Alan Drew. The quickest repartee man in the world. But he was dirty, he didn't clean his stuff up. Milton Berle was dirty, but he cleaned it up when he went somewhere. Alan Drew was filthy. But he could -- somebody heckle him, he'd --
Today we got a guy, what's this guy today that we think is filthy but he's making a big name for himself? You know who I'm talking about?
Out there in Hollywood, that guy? Yeah. He heckled me at Basin Street.
You know who I'm talking about?
You're talking about that black boy.
Yeah, I know -- I can't call his name.
He's got a show on Broadway right now. Let's hold this tape just a minute, because I want to find out his name.
(Recording interrupted.)

-- you mentioned and a lot of other people. When he's great, he's very foul-mouthed; they don't even keep the children go see him. But it was a different era. Nowadays, you can get away with that stuff that Alan Drew couldn't get away with. He'd probably be famous if he were around today, with all of that foul talk. Like Redd Foxx and Richard Pryor is doing.
Oh, Redd Foxx --
Yeah, you know Redd Foxx. What about that?
When Redd Foxx left here, I thought he was through. And then the first thing I know, he's there doing things in Hollywood, up there in Los Angeles.
And he did all those records. You've got them here. Did you like them? You got those records.
Uh-huh, Redd Foxx.
